name: Planning Your Foreclosed Property Renovation Timeline

step.name: Step 1
step.text: Renovating a foreclosed property is an exciting journey, but having a clear timeline is key to keeping things on track. Without one, you might find yourself facing unexpected delays or costs. Here's a look at how we typically approach the process.

step.name: Step 2
step.text: **Phase 1: Initial Assessment & Stabilization.** This starts the moment you get access. We're talking about a comprehensive evaluation of structural integrity, utilities, and moisture. Immediately securing the property, preventing further damage through winterization if needed, and addressing any urgent safety concerns are top priorities here. This phase sets the foundation for everything else.

step.name: Step 3
step.text: **Phase 2: Major System Overhauls.** Once the property is stable, we dive into the big stuff. This includes structural repairs, roof and exterior envelope fixes, and bringing electrical and plumbing systems up to par. This is also when we'd handle any necessary mold remediation. This phase can sometimes uncover more issues, so flexibility is a must.

step.name: Step 4
step.text: **Phase 3: Interior Rough-Ins & Insulation.** With the major systems addressed, we focus on things like insulation, framing changes, and ensuring all the behind-the-walls work is complete before we seal things up. This is a critical point for inspections.

step.name: Step 5
step.text: **Phase 4: Finishes & Cosmetic Updates.** This is where the vision really starts to come to life! Drywall, flooring, painting, cabinetry, and fixture installation happen now. It’s all about creating that "wow" factor and making the home move-in ready. Throughout these phases, open communication is essential to keep you informed every step of the way.
